note: MACS J0416.1-2403 (z=0.396). Instrument: Chandra, ObsIDs 16236, 16237, 16304, 16523 (+others), 0.7-4.0 keV surface-brightness map, 3.94 arcsec pixels. PARAMETRIC MODEL OF THE X-RAY SURFACE BRIGHTNESS, not a tabulated profile and not a deprojected n_e(r). The X-ray surface brightness is modelled as the sum of three SPHERICAL (vanishing ellipticity) dPIE components; the gas density follows from S_X via S_X ~ Lambda(T,Z)/(4 pi (1+z)^4) * integral n_e n_p dz. Centres are offsets in arcsec relative to the NE BCG G1 at RA=04:16:09.154 DEC=-24:04:02.90. Fit performed with Sherpa using the Cash statistic over the inner circular region of radius 40 image pixels ~= 840 kpc, with point sources masked; C=6448, 4914 dof, reduced 1.31. R_T for the two northern components is unconstrained (lower limits only), in which regime the authors note a dPIE profile approaches a beta-model in the central regions. NO core excision. NOTE: this cluster is a pre-merger with a strongly asymmetric, bimodal gas distribution - a spherically averaged profile is a poor description of it.
reference: Bonamigo, Grillo, Ettori, Caminha, Rosati, Mercurio, Annunziatella, Balestra, Lombardi (2017), 'Joining X-Ray to Lensing: An Accurate Combined Analysis of MACS J0416.1-2403', ApJ 842, 132; arXiv:1705.10322, Table 1
caveat: Bimodal merging cluster; the model is a sum of 3 offset spherical components, so it is explicitly NOT a single spherically symmetric profile about one centre.
